Are residual disease, stage and age associated with platinum resistance?

An analysis-ready dataset from The Cancer Genome Atlas ovarian cancer project

Coversheet

Show coversheetHide coversheet
Coversheet

Abstract

Background. Platinum resistance guides retreatment in ovarian cancer, but TCGA-OV holds no documented resistance outcome. This report derived platinum status from dated records with a six-month rule and tested its association with residual disease, stage and age.

Methods. TCGA-OV clinical tables (GDC release 46.0) were quality-assessed. Resistance was a new tumour event within 183 days of the last first-line platinum dose. Outcomes were validated against the TCGA Clinical Data Resource and cBioPortal, and logistic regression was fitted.

Results. Of 491 first-line patients, 366 were modelled and 105 (28.7%) were resistant. Validation targets were met (kappa 0.966). Residual disease of 1 to 10 mm (odds ratio 3.23 (1.62 to 6.95)) and over 10 mm (2.68 (1.26 to 6.04)) and older age (1.29 per 10 years) were associated with resistance.

Conclusion. The dataset suits logistic regression, but the cohort is historical and predominantly white, so the findings are not ready for clinical use.

1 Introduction

Ovarian cancer is the 15th most lethal cancer in the UK, causing around 3,900 deaths a year between 2022 and 2024 (1). For 2022 in England, 62.5% of cases with a known stage were advanced (stage III/IV) (2), while the survival rate for 5 years dropped from 95% for those with stage I to ~15% for those with stage IV (3). Approximately 90% of ovarian cancers are epithelial, which is characterised by being a group of five (or more) histological subtypes differing variously from biology to treatment (4). Of all epithelial ovarian cancers, high grade serous cancer (HGSC) is the most common (4) thought to originate in the fallopian tube (4–6).

The standard first-line treatment involves primary cytoreductive (debulking) surgery (4,7). The surgery is then followed by platinum-based chemotherapy, primarily with cisplatin or carboplatin, usually combined with a taxane (4,7). A key term is the platinum-free interval, which signifies the time from the last platinum dose to a sign of tumour recurrence or progression (4). When the interval is longer, a repeat course of treatment has a higher chance of success: in Markman et al.’s study, 27% of women with an interval of 5 to 12 months responded, while 59% responded after an interval of more than two years (8). If progression occurs within six months of the last platinum dose, the disease is classified as platinum-resistant, whereas if recurrence occurs after six months, it is classified as platinum-sensitive (4). Even though the Gynecologic Cancer InterGroup agreed to replace the then standard platinum-free interval with a therapy-free interval (9), this study focuses on platinum-based treatment, so it uses the platinum-free interval as the measure of resistance. This interval is best measured as a continuous variable (10), and any cut-off point is a convention, so this study also looks at 12 months.

Du Bois et al. took 3,126 patients from three randomised trials and found that covariates such as age, performance status, grade, International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage and histology predicted overall survival (OS) independently of residual disease (11). Complete resection gave the longest progression-free survival and OS, ahead of residual disease of 1 to 10 mm and over 10 mm. However, neither endpoint shows whether the cancer went on to become platinum-resistant.

The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) is a publicly funded project that maps the major genetic changes causing cancer (12). It has profiled and collected clinical data for over 30 cancer types from many tissue source sites (12), and one of its ovarian cancer studies analysed 489 HGSC tumours (13). The clinical tables are open access (14) but vary in quality (15). Liu et al. (16) identified short follow-up, changing recording rules, mixed staging editions and impossible codes such as grade IV ovarian disease (mostly completeness and conformance problems in Kahn’s terms (17)), and they cleaned the data into four survival outcomes, all recommended for ovarian cancer.

Liu et al.’s Clinical Data Resource (CDR) holds no treatment history, and thus cannot show how patients responded to platinum-based treatment (16). Even though cBioPortal provides a platinum status label (sensitive, resistant or too early), the rule that creates it is not recorded in the downloaded data. Nonetheless, it has been used as an outcome, for example to build a resistance predictor on 287 TCGA patients (18). The aim of this report is to build an analysis-ready dataset that derives platinum resistance from dated treatment and disease recurrence records with a stated six-month rule, and to record every patient left out.

Research question. Among patients given first-line platinum, are residual disease, stage and age associated with platinum resistance, and does the association hold at a 12-month cut-off?

2 Methods

2.1 Research question and analytical method

The cohort studied involved patients who started platinum-based treatment within 180 days of diagnosis. Residual disease, FIGO stage group and age at diagnosis were the factors that were tested against platinum resistance. A patient was classed as resistant if their platinum-free interval was shorter than 183 days (six calendar months), meaning a new tumour event occurred less than 183 days after the last first-line dose, or before it. A patient was classed as sensitive if the interval was longer, or if they had 183 days of follow-up without an event. Since the outcome is binary, I chose logistic regression as the method. The dataset fits this method, as it has one row per patient, an outcome derived from dated records, covariates that are fixed before the outcome window, and about 21 events per parameter.

2.2 Data sources and provenance

The TCGA-OV clinical tables (Biospecimen Core Resource (BCR) Biotab, release 46.0) were downloaded from the Genomic Data Commons (GDC) on 11 November 2026 with TCGAbiolinks (19), and a checksum was recorded for each file. Two published resources were used only for validation of the data. The CDR (16) provides curated OS and progression-free interval (PFI) for the same 587 patients (OS missing for 2). The cBioPortal study ov_tcga_pub (13,20,21) provides a platinum status label (sensitive, resistant or too early) for 345 patients. Both were linked on the patient barcode.

2.3 Governance and safety

All sources are open access, and the GDC allows their use in publications when proper accreditation is given (14). The Five Safes (22) guided how the data were handled throughout the study. The TCGA patient barcodes are the only identifiers in the dataset and all times are recorded as days from diagnosis, so the risk of identifying anyone is low. The repository does not include raw data or the intermediate files derived from them, and the report itself contains only counts, summaries and model estimates.

2.4 Data assessment approach

Each of the tables was profiled for various attributes like size, patient coverage and TCGA placeholders such as [Not Available], which were set to missing. Quality checks followed the categories of Kahn et al. (17). Conformance problems included label rows under each header, which meant removing the first two rows of every table, and numbers stored as text. Completeness was assessed further on key patient fields. A range of plausibility checks flagged events after death, negative days, recurrence before the last platinum dose and a few unexpected tumour grade codes (G4 or GB). The vital status conflicted for 47 patients, who were recorded as dead on a follow-up form but alive on the patient form. Finally, implausible values were flagged rather than removed.

2.5 Phenotype definitions and analysis-ready dataset design

Each record (row) is attributed to one patient, with day 0 at diagnosis. Both OS and PFI were rebuilt to check the forms and joins against the CDR. Their follow-up and new tumour event days also feed into the platinum status. First-line platinum treatment was identified from 163 free-text drug names, classified in a lookup table (drug_lookup.csv) and checked individually, row by row. Of the 503 patients given platinum, 483 started within 90 days, so the 180-day cut-off affects only a few patients. There are six ordered rules (phenotypes.md) that assign platinum status, and patients who have no end-date, too little follow-up or who died without recurrence are not classified. Residual disease was grouped as none, 1 to 10 mm or over 10 mm, and stage as I to II, III (reference, the largest group) or IV. Lastly, age was entered per 10 years. The R0 to RX residual field was not taken into consideration because it was missing for the overwhelming majority of the cohort, and the therapy-free interval (9) was not needed, because the focus of this study is specifically treatment with platinum-based drugs, and the platinum part of that interval is the platinum-free interval itself. For all the specifications, see docs/phenotypes.md, docs/data_dictionary.csv and docs/dataset_metadata.md.

2.6 Validation and sensitivity analyses

Validation was taken into consideration by setting agreement targets before any CDR outcome value was viewed, and by adding four expected differences between the CDR and this rebuild before the comparison ran. Both are located in docs/validation_plan.md. OS and PFI were compared with the CDR on event agreement, and OS time on agreement within 30 days. Platinum status was compared with cBioPortal using Cohen’s kappa, because most patients are sensitive, so the two labels would often agree by chance alone. The target of 0.61 marks substantial agreement (23). S1 refits the model at 12 months (24). S2 compares first-line patients in and out of the model. Finally, the model is refitted without the 29 patients in the model whom the CDR marks as redacted, for which the CDR gives no reason.

2.7 Reproducibility

Running run_all.R checks the raw files against their recorded checksums, then runs the numbered scripts in order, each in a new environment. A full rebuild from the raw data has been tested in multiple clean R sessions.

3 Results

3.1 The analysis-ready dataset

The dataset has one row for each of the 587 TCGA-OV patients and 36 columns. Of the 587, 491 started platinum within 180 days of diagnosis. I then excluded from the model 36 with no recorded last dose, 53 who had too little follow-up or died without a recurrence, and 36 missing age, stage or residual disease. That left 366 patients in the model, 105 of whom (28.7%) were platinum-resistant. The CDR (16) marks 45 patients as redacted. Apart from those, very few records were flagged: 11 patients had a recurrence before their last platinum dose and 3 had unexpected tumour grade codes (G4 or GB).

3.2 Validation

All four targets were met (Table 1).

Against the CDR

  • OS events agreed for 584 of the 585 patients in both sources. The exception, recorded as dead with no death day, was one of the differences predicted before the comparison (docs/validation_plan.md).
  • Out of the patients with matching events, 2 had no survival time in one source and 3 differed by more than 30 days.

Against cBioPortal

  • Platinum status agreed for 273 of 277 patients.
  • All four disagreements were resistant here and sensitive in cBioPortal: three recurred 101 to 154 days after their last recorded dose and one before it, which is resistance under the six-month rule, so the difference most likely lies in cBioPortal’s unrecorded rule.
Table 1. Validation against targets set before the comparisons were run
Check Target Achieved Target met
OS event agreement with the CDR 0.95 0.998 yes
OS time within 30 days (matching events) 0.90 0.995 yes
PFI event agreement with the CDR 0.85 0.998 yes
Platinum status: Cohen’s kappa against cBioPortal (277 patients) 0.61 0.966 yes

3.3 Model

Residual disease had the strongest association with resistance (Figure 1). Compared with no macroscopic residual disease, the odds ratio was 3.23 (1.62 to 6.95) for 1 to 10 mm and 2.68 (1.26 to 6.04) for over 10 mm. The intervals overlap widely, so no gradient with size is shown. Also, each 10 years of age was associated with higher odds, 1.29 (1.05 to 1.61). Finally, stage IV did not differ significantly from stage III, 0.82 (0.42 to 1.56). Stage I to II had lower odds, 0.18 (0.01 to 0.94), but only 1 of its 22 patients was resistant, hence the very wide interval.

Figure 1. Odds ratios for platinum resistance at six months, with 95% confidence intervals (366 patients, 105 resistant). Values to the right of 1 mean higher odds of resistance; the axis is on a log scale.

3.4 Sensitivity analyses

  • S1: 12-month cut-off (356 patients, 181 resistant). Both residual disease and age kept their direction with smaller odds ratios, at 2.08 (1.20 to 3.68) for 1 to 10 mm and 1.24 (1.02 to 1.50) per 10 years.
  • Without the redacted patients. Leaving out the 29 redacted patients made little difference: 3.06 (1.52 to 6.65) for 1 to 10 mm and 1.32 (1.05 to 1.66) for age.
  • S2: patients left out (Table 2). The 125 first-line patients left out of the model were similar in age, stage and race but were diagnosed on average about 2 years later.

4 Conclusion

4.1 Fitness for the method

This dataset has been made fit for a logistic regression of platinum resistance, albeit with caveats. When checked, the platinum rule reproduced the cBioPortal label with a kappa of 0.966. This confirms that the method works, but not necessarily that the data are correct, because both use the same TCGA records and a shared error would not be caught. The patients have flags and are not removed, so in_model defines the cohort. The flags allow further exclusions, including the 45 the CDR marks as redacted.

4.2 Uncertainty in the outcome

The platinum-free interval is best used as a continuous measure (10), thus six months is more of a convention than a real cut-off point. At the 12-month point, both residual disease and age kept their directions, but stage IV did not. A death with tumour but no recorded new tumour event does not count as platinum resistance. But a late end-date leads to a shorter interval and pushes the patient towards platinum resistance.

4.3 Selection and representativeness

The main source of bias is the selection process. Firstly, over a quarter of first-line patients (125 of 491) did not qualify because of missing end-dates, short follow-up and/or missing covariates. They were also diagnosed in later calendar years, which led to their shorter observed survival. As a result, the model cohort leaned more towards those who were diagnosed earlier and followed for longer. Race records were missing for 31 patients, and out of the 556 with their race recorded, 498 (89.6%) were white, a heavier skew than the 77% reported across 5,729 samples from ten TCGA tumour types by Spratt et al. (25). Finally, the patient cohort was diagnosed between the years of 1992 and 2013. That means that the treatment is representative of that period, and the findings may not apply to other groups or to current care.

4.4 Governance and FAIR

This dataset carries little to no risk. Under the Five Safes (22), the key risk is in outputs. This is where small cells such as the single resistant patient at stage I to II are reported, though these values are already public.

In regard to the FAIR principles (findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable), the dataset has a fixed name, a source release (GDC 46.0) and a metadata file, and can be rebuilt by anyone using the open GDC data.

4.5 Implications for care

Defining a patient’s platinum status helps clinicians judge which woman is likely to benefit from further platinum-based treatment when her cancer comes back (8). Nonetheless, the cohort is historical and predominantly white, and the results show associations rather than predictions, making them currently unfit for clinical use.

4.6 Future work

Future work could include:

  • modelling the platinum-free interval as a continuous measure, as Bookman et al. recommend (10), or even as a time-to-event outcome;
  • potentially imputing residual disease for the 35 classified patients who were missing it;
  • adding other factors such as BRCA mutation status (9) or homologous recombination status.

Dataset metadata: TCGA-OV platinum response analysis-ready dataset

Dataset: outputs/ard_tcga_ov.csv (587 patients, 36 columns), built from the GDC Biotab clinical tables, data release 46.0, downloaded 11 November 2026.

Abbreviations are listed in abbreviations.md.

Description

I rebuilt this analysis-ready dataset from the raw clinical tables of the 587 TCGA ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma (TCGA-OV) patients. It holds overall survival and the progression-free interval, first-line platinum status at six and twelve months, factors recorded at diagnosis or primary surgery, and quality flags. I built it to test whether residual disease, stage and age are associated with platinum resistance, using logistic regression.

Unit and size

Item Value
Unit of observation one patient, keyed by bcr_patient_barcode
Rows 587
Columns 36
On first-line platinum (platinum_status not blank) 491
In the model (in_model is TRUE) 366 (105 resistant, 261 sensitive)

Patients are flagged, not removed: everyone stays in the file, and in_model marks the model cohort.

Ethnicity is recorded for 350 patients (59.6%); 11 of them are Hispanic or Latino. Mean age at diagnosis is about 60 (outputs/cbio_coverage.csv). Patients were diagnosed between 1992 and 2013 (median 2004), and the last follow-up form was completed on 31 July 2015 (docs/data_sources.md).

Missing values

Missing values are blank in the CSV (NA in R). I set the five TCGA placeholders ([Not Available], [Not Applicable], [Unknown], [Not Evaluated] and [Discrepancy]) to blank in 02_clean.R. The dictionary gives the count of blanks for every column.

Time convention

All times are whole days since initial pathologic diagnosis (day 0). A negative value means before diagnosis: negative survival or new tumour event days are flagged (flag_negative_days; none found), and one patient’s platinum starts on day -8.

Validation summary

Check Target Achieved
OS event agreement with the CDR 0.95 0.998
OS time within 30 days, matching events 0.90 0.995
PFI event agreement with the CDR 0.85 0.998
Platinum status, Cohen’s kappa against cBioPortal 0.61 0.966

I set and dated the targets in docs/validation_plan.md before running either comparison. Linkage was by exact match on bcr_patient_barcode: all 587 patients matched the CDR, and all 345 cBioPortal patients matched with no duplicates. Patients with a cBioPortal label are similar to those without on age, stage, residual disease and diagnosis year, but more often white (92.3% vs 85.4% of those with race recorded).

How to rebuild

  1. Clone the repository and open HDS_M1_TCGA_OV.Rproj in RStudio.
  2. Run renv::restore() to install the package versions I used.
  3. Source run_all.R. It runs 00_data_download.R, which downloads all three sources (the GDC Biotab tables, the CDR table and the cBioPortal label), then the numbered scripts in order. A fresh download gets the current GDC release; this dataset used release 46.0, and later releases may differ.
  4. Knit reports/report.Rmd in RStudio.

The raw and intermediate data (data/raw/ and data/derived/) are not stored in the repository; the scripts rebuild them. Full instructions are in the README.

FAIR

Principle How this dataset meets it
Findable a fixed name and source release (GDC 46.0); this file and the dictionary describe it; keywords below
Accessible built only from open-access GDC data; anyone can download the source and rebuild it with the scripts
Interoperable plain CSV; TCGA barcodes, the same key the GDC, CDR and cBioPortal use; source column names kept in the dictionary; ICD-10 and FIGO stage values kept as recorded
Reusable every column described with its source, rule and window; derivations specified in phenotypes.md; validation results recorded; flagged patients kept so others can choose their own exclusions

Five Safes

Safe How it applies to this dataset
Safe projects I built it to answer one stated question, whether residual disease, stage and age are associated with platinum resistance, as part of the Cambridge MSt in Healthcare Data Science. The GDC allows its open-access data to be used in publications with proper accreditation.
Safe people I am the only analyst, and I have completed the Medical Research Council (MRC) course Confidentiality and Data Protection in Health Research, passing the quiz on 24 October 2026 (certificate).
Safe settings I did the work on a personal computer. The raw and intermediate data (data/raw/ and data/derived/) are kept out of Git, and the scripts, documentation and outputs are published in a public GitHub repository.
Safe data I used only open-access GDC clinical data, with no controlled-access data. TCGA barcodes are the only identifiers and every time interval is counted in days from diagnosis; age, race and diagnosis year are kept as the public source records them.
Safe outputs The report shows only counts, percentages, summary statistics and model estimates. One cell is very small (1 resistant patient of 22 at stage I to II), which would usually be suppressed; I report it because the source is already public. The dataset itself is patient-level, but it holds nothing beyond what the GDC already publishes, so sharing it adds little disclosure risk.

Framework: Desai, Ritchie and Welpton (2016).

Keywords

TCGA, ovarian cancer, high-grade serous, platinum resistance, platinum-free interval, overall survival, progression-free interval, analysis-ready dataset

Licence and attribution

The source data are NCI GDC open-access data, which the GDC states can be used in publications or presentations with proper accreditation. Reuse should credit the TCGA Research Network and the NCI Genomic Data Commons.

Known limitations

  • Representativeness. This is a research cohort, not a population sample. Of the 556 patients with race recorded, 89.6% are white and 6.1% Black, and ethnicity is missing for 40.4%, so results may not apply to other groups. Spratt et al. (2016) report the same pattern across TCGA.
  • Treatment era. Patients were diagnosed between 1992 and 2013 (median 2004) and followed up to July 2015 at the latest, so treatment reflects that period.
  • Data collection. Follow-up and collection rules varied between sites, and stage was recorded under the FIGO version each site used (Liu et al. 2018).
  • Treatment history. The dataset captures only first-line treatment, so the therapy-free interval now preferred by the GCIG cannot be built from it (Wilson et al. 2017).
  • Drug coding. Drug names are free text. I classified them in a lookup table, drug_lookup.csv, and checked every row, rather than mapping them to a standard code system.
  • Data quality. I kept and flagged implausible values rather than removing them; the flags are listed in the dictionary.
  • Validation. Agreement with the CDR and cBioPortal shows that my rules reproduce published derivations, not that the source forms are correct.
  • Redaction. The CDR marks 45 patients as redacted without giving a reason. I kept and flagged them (flag_cdr_redacted), so users can leave them out.

Variable-level limitations are in docs/phenotypes.md.

Download

  • The data were downloaded on 11 November 2026 using scripts/00_data_download.R
  • Software used was R 4.6.1 and TCGAbiolinks 2.40.0 (the full list is in data/manifests/session_info.txt)
  • Checksums are saved in data/manifests/download_record.csv and the GDC file list in data/manifests/gdc_files.csv
  • GitHub repository: https://github.com/sergiovasileiou/HDS_M1_TCGA_OV_PUBLIC (public)

Time period

  • GDC data release: 46.0 (10 August 2026), current on the download date
  • Patients were diagnosed between 1992 and 2013. 486 of 587 (82.8%) were diagnosed between 2000 and 2009, with the median year being 2004. There were no missing years.
  • Patient forms were completed between 19 February 2009 and 1 October 2014
  • Follow-up forms were completed between 19 February 2009 and 31 July 2015, so no follow-ups after mid-2015 are included
  • All form completion dates could be read as dates (quality check)
  • How data were collected (prospective or retrospective) is recorded for only 17 of 587 patients (11 retrospective, 6 prospective), missing for 570 (97.1%)
  • The CDR was published in 2018 (Liu et al. 2018); the cBioPortal study goes with the 2011 TCGA ovarian paper (TCGA Research Network 2011)

How the tables connect

Every table carries both patient identifiers: bcr_patient_uuid and bcr_patient_barcode. The tables can be joined on either, but the barcode will be used, as it is the identifier shared with the CDR and cBioPortal and is written the same way in every table. All days are counted from diagnosis.

First observations

Structure

  • Each table has two label rows under the header, the first repeats the column names and the second holds CDE_ID codes
  • Every column is stored as text, including ages and day counts
  • All days are counted from diagnosis, as days_to_initial_pathologic_diagnosis is 0 for all 587 patients
  • Column naming differs between tables, for example days_to_radiation_therapy_start against pharmaceutical_tx_started_days_to
  • Formats vary within columns, with dates written without leading zeros (2009-3-26) and cycle counts written as both 06 and 4

Missing values

  • Missing values are written as text, such as [Not Available], [Not Applicable] and [Unknown]
  • Residual disease is recorded in two fields. residual_disease_largest_nodule is missing for 67 patients and residual_tumor (R0 to RX) for 529

Patients

  • There are 587 patients, with one row each and no duplicate barcodes
  • 302 patients were recorded as dead, 282 as alive and 3 were not available
  • Most patients were stage IIIC (413) or IV (89). Stage I had 17 patients, stage II 30, IIIA and IIIB 33, and 5 were not available
  • For residual disease (largest nodule), 120 patients had none, 256 had 1-10 mm, 38 had 11-20 mm and 106 had over 20 mm, with 67 not available
  • Race and ethnicity are recorded, so the make-up of the cohort can be described

Follow-up and new tumour events

  • 496 patients had one follow-up form, 80 had two and 4 had three or four, while 7 had none
  • Vital status differs between the tables. 344 patients were marked dead in at least one follow-up form (346 rows, as 2 patients had two), compared with 302 in the patient table. 297 patients were dead in both, 47 were dead in follow-up only and 5 in the patient table only, so 349 patients were recorded as dead somewhere. All 47 were marked “Alive” in the patient table, so the two tables contradict each other for these patients
  • New tumour events are split across two tables (513 and 8 rows). The follow-up version has one extra column, bcr_followup_barcode, so the tables were combined with bind_rows(). Across both, there were 297 recurrences, 64 locoregional, 42 metastatic, 42 progression, 4 both locoregional and distant, and 72 unknown
  • TCGA-59-A5PD has two new tumour event records on day 145 (one Recurrence, one [Unknown]), which may be the same event recorded twice

Drugs

  • There are 2,516 drug records for 530 patients, while 57 patients had no drug record
  • By therapy type, there were 2,382 chemotherapy, 60 targeted, 51 hormone and 17 immunotherapy records, with 6 not available
  • Drug names are free text with variant spellings, such as Taxol, Paclitaxel and Paciltaxel, Gemcitabine, Gemzar and Gemcitibine, and Carboplatin and Carbo
  • Some entries name two drugs in one field (Taxol/Carboplatin, Topotecan/Carboplatin, Cisplatin/Gemzar), and each combined entry appears only once
  • Some entries come from blinded trials, so the drug actually given is unknown (Bevacizamab/Placebo, Ovarex/placebo, spellings as recorded)
  • A therapy_regimen column records why each drug was given (ADJUVANT, RECURRENCE)
  • The drug names were later classified in data/lookup/drug_lookup.csv and checked row by row (Step 12)

Other tables

  • There were 36 radiotherapy records for 34 patients. This table is not used
  • 3 patients had a second cancer diagnosed at the same time. This table is not used

Other sources

TCGA-CDR (Liu et al. 2018)

  • The CDR holds 11,160 patients across all TCGA cancers, 587 of them ovarian, all of which matched Biotab (confirmed by 06_validate_cdr.R on 18 Nov)
  • It has eight sheets, with the patient data on the sheet “TCGA-CDR”
  • There is one row per patient, and it joins to Biotab on the patient barcode
  • The outcome columns, as defined by Liu et al. 2018, are:
    • OS and OS.time, overall survival from diagnosis to death from any cause. Patients still alive are censored at their last contact
    • PFI and PFI.time, the progression-free interval from diagnosis to the first new tumour event (progression, locoregional recurrence, distant metastasis, new primary tumour) or death with tumour. Patients alive without an event, or who died without tumour, are censored
    • OS and PFI are the event indicators, while OS.time and PFI.time are the days
  • The Redaction column shows whether a case is redacted. The CDR’s notes sheet (TCGA-CDR_Notes) gives no reason; 45 ovarian patients are marked Redacted, and they are kept in the dataset with flag_cdr_redacted
  • It is used only as a reference to check the rebuilt OS and PFI. The outcome values were first compared on 18 Nov, after the targets in docs/validation_plan.md were set
  • It was curated from the same TCGA clinical records, so it is not fully independent

cBioPortal ov_tcga_pub (TCGA 2011)

  • It holds 345 patients, 197 sensitive, 90 resistant and 58 too early (recorded as “Tooearly”)
  • There were no duplicate patient IDs, and all 345 were found in the Biotab patient table
  • It is used only as a reference to check the derived platinum status
  • It comes from an earlier data freeze with its own definition, and covers 345 of the 587 patients

Phenotype specifications: TCGA-OV platinum response analysis-ready dataset

Dataset: outputs/ard_tcga_ov.csv (587 patients, 36 columns), built from the GDC Biotab clinical tables, data release 46.0, downloaded 11 November 2026.

Abbreviations are listed in abbreviations.md.

Day 0 for every phenotype is the date of initial pathologic diagnosis; every day field in the Biotab tables counts from it. Counts are from the run of 18 November 2026.

Overview

Phenotype Variables Population Role Code Checked against Result

Progression-free interval pfi_event, pfi_days all 587 check on the recurrence date 03_survival.R TCGA-CDR, event agreement 0.998 413 events

1. Overall survival (os_event, os_days)

Purpose. Not used in the model. Rebuilt from the raw forms to check the pipeline: the CDR built the same endpoint independently, so close agreement shows the patient and follow-up forms were cleaned and joined correctly before the platinum outcome was built from the same days.

Field Detail
Population all 587 patients
Index date diagnosis (day 0)
Outcome window any time in follow-up
Event a death day on the patient form or any follow-up form
Censoring latest last contact day, for patients without a death day; no follow-up after 31 July 2015, the last form completed
Source fields death_days_to and last_contact_days_to in clinical_patient_ov and clinical_follow_up_v1.0_ov
Repeat observations one patient form and any number of follow-up forms per patient, combined into one row
Quality flags flag_death_conflict, flag_dead_no_date, flag_followup_after_death, flag_no_time, flag_negative_days
Provenance death_source: both forms 296, follow-up form only 47, patient form only 5 (outputs/source_summary.csv)
Code scripts/03_survival.R, sections 1 to 3 and 7

Rule. os_event is 1 if any form has a death day, otherwise 0. os_days is the death day for events and the latest last contact day for everyone else.

Missing or conflicting data. If forms give different death days, the earliest is used and flagged. Dead with no death day: not an event, flagged. No death day or last contact day: os_days blank, flagged. Nobody is removed.

Result. 348 events; os_days blank for 3 patients.

Checked against TCGA-CDR (Liu et al. 2018) OS and OS.time (scripts/06_validate_cdr.R):

Measure Target Achieved
Event agreement 0.95 0.998 (584 of 585)
Time within 30 days, matching events 0.90 0.995 (579 of 582)

Of the 5 patients with matching events but no time agreement, 3 differ by over 30 days and 2 have no time in one source. The one event disagreement is the patient recorded as dead with no death day (expected difference 2). Two patients have no OS value in the CDR.

Known limitations.

  • Follow-up. Collected unevenly across sites, so patients are censored at very different points and a death after the last form would be missed.
  • Missing dates. The patient recorded as dead with no death day counts as alive here, and the 3 patients with no usable time cannot enter a time-based analysis.
  • Validation. Agreement with the CDR shows two derivations match, not that the forms are correct, because both start from the same TCGA records.

2. Progression-free interval (pfi_event, pfi_days)

Purpose. Not used in the model. Checked against the CDR because its first new tumour event day is the recurrence date the platinum outcome is built on. If PFI matches an independent derivation, those recurrence dates can be trusted.

Field Detail
Population all 587 patients
Index date diagnosis (day 0)
Outcome window any time in follow-up
Event the first new tumour event in either new tumour event table, or death while recorded as with tumour on any form
Competing event death with no tumour recorded; not an event, censored at os_days
Censoring os_days, for patients with no event
Source fields new_tumor_event_dx_days_to in clinical_nte_ov and clinical_follow_up_v1.0_nte_ov; tumor_status in clinical_patient_ov and clinical_follow_up_v1.0_ov; os_event and os_days
Repeat observations several new tumour events across the two tables; only the earliest is used
Quality flags flag_nte_after_death, flag_negative_days
Provenance nte_source: the first event came from the follow-up table for 359 patients and the separate table for 3 (outputs/source_summary.csv)
Code scripts/03_survival.R, sections 4, 5, 8 and 10

Rule. pfi_event is 1 if either table has a new tumour event, or if the patient died and any form says WITH TUMOR; otherwise 0. pfi_days is the day of the earliest new tumour event, or os_days if there is none.

Missing or conflicting data. If tumour status is missing on every form, a death does not count as an event (27 patients). A new tumour event with no day is not used.

Result. 413 events. 34 deaths are not events: 7 were recorded tumour-free and 27 have no tumour status on any form (outputs/death_no_pfi.csv).

Checked against TCGA-CDR (Liu et al. 2018) PFI (scripts/06_validate_cdr.R):

Measure Target Achieved
Event agreement 0.85 0.998 (586 of 587)

The one disagreement is an event in the CDR that is not an event here.

Known limitations.

  • Missing tumour status. 27 patients who died have no tumour status on any form, so their deaths cannot count; if any died with tumour, events are undercounted (a completeness problem in Kahn’s terms).
  • Two source tables. New tumour events sit in two tables with different columns; both are used, and nte_source records which one each first event came from.
  • Validation. Agreement with the CDR shows two derivations match, but both use the same forms, so a recurrence that was never recorded is missing from both.

3. Platinum status at six months (platinum_status)

Purpose. The outcome of the logistic regression. It turns the dated drug and new tumour event records into the six-month split clinicians use to judge whether platinum is likely to work again, so that residual disease, stage and age can be tested against it.

Field Detail
Population patients whose platinum drug started within 180 days of diagnosis: 491 of 587; blank for the other 96
Index date diagnosis (day 0)
Exposure window platinum started on day 180 or earlier (see the note under this table)
Outcome window from the last first-line platinum dose (last_platinum_days)
Source fields pharmaceutical_therapy_drug_name, pharmaceutical_tx_started_days_to and pharmaceutical_tx_ended_days_to in clinical_drug_ov; the first new tumour event day; os_days and os_event
Code list data/lookup/drug_lookup.csv: 163 drug names as written in the raw table, each marked platinum yes or no and given a drug group, checked by hand
Drug decisions oxaliplatin counts as platinum (3 patients); other hand-checked entries are explained in the notes column of drug_lookup.csv
Repeat observations several platinum rows per patient; the earliest start, latest end and highest cycle count among first-line rows are used
Quality flags flag_recur_before_last_dose (11 patients, classed resistant)
Code scripts/04_treatment.R, sections 1 to 6

Exposure window. Of 503 patients with any platinum, 483 started within 90 days, 8 between days 91 and 180 and 12 later, so the cut-off falls in a sparse stretch and moving it would change few patients (outputs/platinum_start_days.csv).

Rule. Checked in order; the first match is used.

Order Status Condition
1 no end date a first-line platinum row has no end day
2 resistant new tumour event less than 183 days after the last dose, including one before the last dose
3 sensitive new tumour event 183 days or more after the last dose
4 sensitive no new tumour event, and followed for at least 183 days after the last dose
5 died without recurrence no new tumour event, and died within 183 days of the last dose
6 too early everyone else: alive, no new tumour event, followed for under 183 days

Only a new tumour event counts as recurrence. A death with tumour but no new tumour event counts for PFI but falls under rule 4 or 5 here, not rule 2.

Missing or conflicting data. A first-line platinum row with no end day: no end date (36 patients), not classified. Drug rows with no drug name: not matched (10 rows).

Result. 111 resistant, 291 sensitive, 43 too early, 36 no end date and 10 died without recurrence. The table under entry 4 compares both cut-offs.

Checked against cBioPortal study ov_tcga_pub (TCGA, Nature 2011; paper), attribute PLATINUM_STATUS (scripts/07_validate_platinum.R). 335 of the 345 labelled patients had first-line platinum here.

cBioPortal resistant cBioPortal sensitive cBioPortal too early
Resistant here 85 4 3
Sensitive here 0 188 20
Too early here 0 0 34
No end date here 1 0 0

Of the 277 classed resistant or sensitive in both sources, 273 agree (0.986); Cohen’s kappa 0.966 (target 0.61). Patients with a cBioPortal label are similar to those without on age, stage, residual disease and diagnosis year, but more often white (92.3% vs 85.4% of those with race recorded) and less often missing race (2.3% vs 9.5%), so the comparison rests on a less diverse subset (outputs/cbio_coverage.csv).

Known limitations.

  • Cut-off. Six months is a clinical convention, not a biological boundary; Bookman et al. (2017) describe the interval as best reported as a continuous measure, so patients either side of 183 days may differ little. Six months is taken as 183 days (six calendar months). A post hoc check with 180 days moves 2 model patients (TCGA-09-0365 and TCGA-25-2393, intervals of 181 and 182 days) from resistant to sensitive; residual disease barely changes, but the age interval then includes 1 (scripts/08_model.R, section 7; outputs/model_180.csv).
  • Missing end-dates. 36 patients (7.3% of first-line patients) have no end-date and cannot be classified.
  • Implausible dates. 11 recurred before their last dose and 3 have end-dates after day 365; a late end-date shortens the interval and pushes a patient towards resistant.
  • Recurrence rule. A patient who died with tumour but has no new tumour event recorded cannot be classed resistant.
  • Validation. Agreement with cBioPortal shows this rule reproduces the published label, but that label’s rule is not documented, so agreement cannot show which rule is right.

4. Platinum status at twelve months (platinum_status_12m), sensitivity analysis S1

Purpose. Sensitivity analysis S1. Repeats the model with a 12-month cut-off to test whether the six-month results depend on where the line is drawn. Twelve months separates the group Dockery et al. (2019) call partially platinum sensitive (recurrence at 6 to 12 months, worse prognosis) from later recurrences, in whom platinum works best.

Field Detail
Population, index date, windows, source fields, code list as for platinum_status
Rule the same six rules, with 365 days in place of 183 in rules 2 to 5
Code scripts/04_treatment.R, section 7
Checked against no published label uses 12 months; used to test whether the model results depend on the cut-off (scripts/08_model.R). In the 12-month model (356 patients, 181 resistant), residual disease and age kept the same direction as at six months, with smaller odds ratios

Result, both cut-offs (491 first-line platinum patients):

Status 6 months 12 months
sensitive 291 196
resistant 111 193
too early 43 54
no end date 36 36
died without recurrence 10 12

Known limitations.

  • No outside check. No published label uses 12 months.
  • Follow-up needed. Patients need a year of follow-up after their last dose to be classed sensitive without a recurrence, so too early rises from 43 to 54.
  • Mixed resistant group. Resistant rises from 111 to 193: the 82 extra patients recurred between 6 and 12 months, so resistant here mixes two groups clinicians would treat differently.
  • Inherited limitations. The data limitations of platinum_status still apply: 36 with no end-date, and death with tumour is not counted as recurrence.

Validation plan: TCGA-OV platinum response analysis-ready dataset

Dataset: outputs/ard_tcga_ov.csv (587 patients, 36 columns), built from the GDC Biotab clinical tables, data release 46.0, downloaded 11 November 2026.

Abbreviations are listed in abbreviations.md.

Written on the 13th of November, before viewing any outcome values in the TCGA-CDR. Only the sheet name and column names had been read, which confirmed that the same 587 ovarian patients appear in both sources. From cBioPortal, only the counts of its platinum label had been seen (Sensitive 197, Resistant 90, Tooearly 58), not how they compare with my own classification.

Overall survival

  • Agreement with the CDR events: at least 95% of patients in both sources
  • Time within 30 days of the CDR: at least 90% of patients with matching events

Progression-free interval

  • Agreement: at least 85%. Lower agreement is expected because PFI depends on new tumour event dates from two tables, which are not as filled as death dates

Platinum status against cBioPortal

  • Cohen’s kappa of at least 0.61 (substantial on the Landis and Koch scale)
  • Calculated only on patients labelled sensitive or resistant in both sources. Patients classed as too early, died without recurrence or with no end-date in my data, and as Tooearly in cBioPortal, are left out, and the number in each group is reported

Disagreements

  • Every disagreement is grouped by reason, and up to 10 per group are traced back to the raw rows
  • I will not change a rule only to improve agreement

Expected differences (added 18 November 2026, before running the CDR comparison)

From the CDR’s notes on how its endpoints were derived, read before viewing any outcome values:

  1. OS time: the CDR takes the larger of last contact and death day; this rebuild takes the death day.
  2. Dead with no death day: likely an event in the CDR; not an event here, because there is no time.
  3. Tumour status: the CDR uses the latest status; this rebuild uses “with tumour” on any form.
  4. New tumour events: the CDR uses the follow-up files; this rebuild also uses the separate new tumour event table.

Changes made after validation

  • 18 November 2026: the decisions on seven flagged entries in data/lookup/drug_lookup.csv were finalised after 06_validate_cdr.R and 07_validate_platinum.R had been run. Two trial entries (GOG 218 and GOG182) were changed to platinum because every arm of those trials gave carboplatin. The reasons are recorded in the notes column. No patient count, agreement figure or kappa changed.

Abbreviations

Abbreviation Meaning
BCR Biospecimen Core Resource; the BCR Biotab files are TCGA’s clinical tables
BRCA BRCA1 and BRCA2, the breast cancer susceptibility genes
CDR TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource (Liu et al. 2018), also written TCGA-CDR
CI Confidence interval
CSV Comma-separated values (file format)
FAIR Findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable
FIGO International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (staging system)
G4, GB Tumour grade codes not expected in this cohort; flagged by flag_grade_check
GCIG Gynecologic Cancer InterGroup
GDC Genomic Data Commons, run by the NCI
GOG Gynecologic Oncology Group (trial names such as GOG 218)
HGSC High-grade serous carcinoma
ICD-10 International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision
MRC Medical Research Council
MSt Master of Studies
NA Not available: a missing value in R
NCI National Cancer Institute (United States)
OR Odds ratio
OS Overall survival
PFI Progression-free interval, as defined in the CDR. The platinum-free interval is always written in full
PMID PubMed identifier
R0, RX Residual tumour codes: R0, no residual tumour; RX, residual tumour cannot be assessed
S1, S2 Sensitivity analyses: S1, 12-month cut-off; S2, patients in and out of the model
TCGA The Cancer Genome Atlas
TCGA-OV TCGA ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma project
